**Why coverage was added:** PR #1754 added regression tests for the 401 handling in `openmrsFetch`. Its summary says the 401 redirect path had no tests. The PR links to ticket O3-5629.

**What the new tests pin down** (all in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.test.ts`, lines 166-214):

- **401 with a `Location` header** (lines 166-185): `navigate` is called with `{ to: <Location value> }`, so the server's auth-module challenge URL is followed. The test sets `redirectAuthFailure.url` to `''` so the header is the only source.
- **401 without a `Location` header** (lines 197-214): `navigate` goes to the default login URL, `${openmrsSpaBase}/login`. The test also sets `url` to `''`.

The wrapper logic these tests exercise is in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.ts`, lines 225-243. The target is chosen in this order: the configured `redirectAuthFailure.url`, then the response's `Location` header, then `defaultRedirectAuthFailureUrl` (line 234). The question's wording says the configured page is used only when there is no redirect target. The code actually checks the configured URL first, so the `Location` header only applies when that URL is blank.

Two other tests in the same file cover nearby behavior. Lines 216-233 check that a configured `url` is used on a 401. Lines 235-243 check `rejectAuthFailure`. I did not confirm which of these were added by #1754 versus earlier, because I only had the PR's file stats (63 additions, 1 deletion) and not its diff.

**Which change and ticket:** the test commit is `e16e2d9e` ("(test) Add regression tests for 401 Location-header redirect in openmrsFetch (#1754)"), merged 2026-05-01. The ticket is O3-5629. The related session-endpoint redirect on success (lines 187-195 of `openmrs-fetch.ts`) came from commit `9dae818f` (#1797, O3-5767). That is a different path, so I listed it as supporting evidence only.

I only read the code and history; I did not run the test suite.
